findings.location: <harness-onion>/scripts/evolution_surface.py tree_paths and check_coverage; README 'Programme paths' symbolic-link paragraph (lines 136-138) and the COVERAGE row
findings.finding: The rewritten walk tests the skip set before it tests for a link, and _skipped is applied to every listed link. So _gate_link never judges a symbolic link whose name is a skip-set directory (__pycache__, .pytest_cache, .ruff_cache or .mypy_cache at any depth; .git or .venv at the root) or matches a skip-set file pattern (*.py[cod], .DS_Store). Each of these passes check_coverage on scratch trees: a link ci/__pycache__ -> ../docs/cache (a gate path serving a data directory); a link ci/real.cpython-312.pyc -> a data .pyc; a link ci/.DS_Store -> a data file; a data link docs/__pycache__ -> ../ci; a root .venv -> ci. The same ci/__pycache__ link pointing at a data file is refused, so the outcome depends on the target's type even though links are 'never followed'. Round 1's walk listed ci/__pycache__ as a file; this change drops it. README lines 136-137 and the COVERAGE row promise a refusal. These are Python's bytecode-cache names. An unchecked hash-based .pyc in a gate directory's __pycache__ is imported without reading its source, so such a link would let data-only PRs change bytecode that gate code loads. MINOR, not MAJOR: adding the link itself changes a gate path, and pr_approvers then gives [OWNER], so the owner's per-PR approval still stands in front. The link rule is the backstop, and it misses this case.
findings.requiredChange: Judge every symbolic link the walk meets with the link rule, whatever its name; the skip set should only skip classification. For example, test for a link before testing the skip set, keep root .git or .venv links unclassified but judged, and keep _skipped from removing a link from the link check. State this in the README. Add tests for a gate-path link named __pycache__ to a data directory, a gate-path link named *.pyc, and a data link named __pycache__ to a gate directory.

findings.finding: _gate_link judges a link's target by how it is spelled relative to the root, not by what it reaches. (a) A target that is an ancestor of the root contains the tree's gate material. But its relative path is '..' or starts with '../', so the link is accepted: docs/up -> ../.. passes, while docs/all -> .. (the root) is refused. README line 137 ('whose final target lies in or contains gate material inside the tree') covers this case. (b) os.path.realpath keeps the spelling of components that are not links, and _matches is case-sensitive. So on a case-insensitive file system (the macOS default; the scratch volume here is one), data links docs/caps -> ../CI, docs/caps2 -> ../CI/real.py and docs/caps3 -> ../Docs/harnesses reach ci/ and docs/harnesses/ but pass check_coverage. Both cases concern the data-link half of the rule. A link's own path comes from the walk's on-disk names and is not affected.
findings.requiredChange: Refuse a link when the resolved root equals or lies inside the resolved target. Judge the target by identity rather than spelling: for example, compare the os.stat st_dev and st_ino of the target and each of its ancestors with the on-disk gate entries, use os.path.samefile, or case-fold on a case-insensitive file system. Add a test for each case.

findings.location: <harness-onion>/architecture/evolution-surface/vectors.json consumer case K11; README 'Activation', programme level (line 82)
findings.finding: K11 ('main moved after the verify, before the merge') expects 'no merge; the head is verified again on current main'. Neither Q-ES-D3 (a) as DESIGN.md section 10 states it nor MONITOR.md section 4 gives that remedy. MONITOR.md says 'On any mismatch, stop, record and report to the owner'. Admission rule 2, which the README cites (the head contains current main), makes a re-verify of the same head fail whenever main moved past the head's base. A new head and a new approval are then needed (README line 69). The 'no merge' part is right; the remedy is inexact and leaves out the stop, record and report. The README's line 82 applies stop, record and report only to a tree mismatch. That follows the design's wording, which the owner accepted, but MONITOR.md's practice is broader.
findings.requiredChange: Change K11's expected outcome to: no merge; the monitor stops, records it and reports to the owner; a merge needs a verify whose main sha equals current main, on a head that contains it (a re-pushed head needs a new approval). Optionally, align README line 82 with MONITOR.md's 'any mismatch'.

findings.location: <harness-onion>/architecture/evolution-surface/README.md (Files table, line 28; COVERAGE row; line 137); <harness-onion>/scripts/evolution_surface.py check_paths, _gate_link and tree_paths; vectors.json invariants
findings.finding: (a) The Files table says '10 request refusals', but U10 expects null (a pass): there are 9 refusals and 1 pass. The disposition table's 'ten request vectors' is right. (b) check_paths does not apply the skip set, but the COVERAGE row reads 'outside the skip set (check_paths, check_coverage)'. A list holding a root .DS_Store, .venv/x or a/__pycache__/m.pyc is refused by check_paths, while check_coverage would skip those paths; docs/x.pyc passes as data. This is stricter, not weaker. (c) An entry whose lstat fails is treated as not a link. In a directory that can be listed but not searched (mode r--r--r--), a link to ../../ci is listed as a data file and passes check_coverage. This is an environment fault, like G1R1-1, and a PR tree cannot create it. (d) The README's reason ('a data-only change to the target would change what a gate path serves') fits only links at gate paths. The data-link half needs its own reason (a data path that aliases gate material). (e) I29 to I31 sit before I28 in vectors.json. A linked root is refused, which line 299's rule ('not an existing directory') does not state.
findings.requiredChange: Fix the count in the Files table. Say that check_paths takes an already filtered list, or apply the skip set there. Refuse COVERAGE when lstat of a listed entry fails. Give the data-link half its own reason. Optionally, reorder I28 and state the linked-root refusal.
